title: תהילים פרק 118
english_audio_source: YouVersion — The Listener’s Bible®: KJV Edition
verses: ״הוֹדוּ לַיהוָה כִּי טוֹב: כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ.״
״יֹאמַר נָא יִשְׂרָאֵל: כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ.״
״יֹאמְרוּ נָא בֵית אַהֲרֹן: כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ.״
״יֹאמְרוּ נָא יִרְאֵי יְהוָה: כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ.״
״מִן הַמֵּצַר קָרָאתִי יָּהּ. עָנָנִי בַמֶּרְחָב יָהּ.״
״יְהוָה לִי לֹא אִירָא. מַה יַּעֲשֶׂה לִי אָדָם.״
״יְהוָה לִי בְּעֹזְרָי. וַאֲנִי, אֶרְאֶה בְשֹׂנְאָי.״
״טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּיהוָה. מִבְּטֹחַ, בָּאָדָם.״
״טוֹב לַחֲסוֹת בַּיהוָה. מִבְּטֹחַ, בִּנְדִיבִים.״
״כָּל גּוֹיִם סְבָבוּנִי. בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה כִּי אֲמִילַם.״
״סַבּוּנִי גַם סְבָבוּנִי. בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה כִּי אֲמִילַם.״
״סַבּוּנִי כִדְבוֹרִים. דֹּעֲכוּ כְּאֵשׁ קוֹצִים. בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה, כִּי אֲמִילַם.״
״דַּחֹה דְחִיתַנִי לִנְפֹּל. וַיהוָה עֲזָרָנִי.״
״עָזִּי וְזִמְרָת יָהּ. וַיְהִי לִי לִישׁוּעָה.״
״קוֹל רִנָּה וִישׁוּעָה. בְּאָהֳלֵי צַדִּיקִים. יְמִין יְהוָה, עֹשָׂה חָיִל.״
״יְמִין יְהוָה רוֹמֵמָה. יְמִין יְהוָה, עֹשָׂה חָיִל.״
״לֹא אָמוּת כִּי אֶחְיֶה. וַאֲסַפֵּר מַעֲשֵׂי יָהּ.״
״יַסֹּר יִסְּרַנִּי יָּהּ. וְלַמָּוֶת לֹא נְתָנָנִי.״
״פִּתְחוּ לִי שַׁעֲרֵי צֶדֶק. אָבֹא בָם אוֹדֶה יָהּ.״
״זֶה הַשַּׁעַר לַיהוָה. צַדִּיקִים יָבֹאוּ בוֹ.״
״אוֹדְךָ כִּי עֲנִיתָנִי. וַתְּהִי לִי, לִישׁוּעָה.״
״אֶבֶן מָאֲסוּ הַבּוֹנִים. הָיְתָה, לְרֹאשׁ פִּנָּה.״
״מֵאֵת יְהוָה הָיְתָה זֹּאת. הִיא נִפְלָאת בְּעֵינֵינוּ.״
״זֶה הַיּוֹם עָשָׂה יְהוָה. נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בוֹ.״
״אָנָּא יְהוָה הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא. אָנָּא יְהוָה, הַצְלִיחָה נָּא.״
״בָּרוּךְ הַבָּא בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה. בֵּרַכְנוּכֶם, מִבֵּית יְהוָה.״
״אֵל, יְהוָה. וַיָּאֶר לָנוּ: אִסְרוּ חַג בַּעֲבֹתִים. עַד קַרְנוֹת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.״
״אֵלִי אַתָּה וְאוֹדֶךָּ. אֱלֹהַי אֲרוֹמְמֶךָּ.״
״הוֹדוּ לַיהוָה כִּי טוֹב: כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ.״
english: O give thanks unto the LORD ; for he is good: because his mercy endureth for ever.
Let Israel now say, that his mercy endureth for ever.
Let the house of Aaron now say, that his mercy endureth for ever.
Let them now that fear the LORD say, that his mercy endureth for ever.
I called upon the LORD in distress: the LORD answered me, and set me in a large place.
The LORD is on my side; I will not fear: what can man do unto me?
The LORD taketh my part with them that help me: therefore shall I see my desire upon them that hate me.
It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in man.
It is better to trust in the LORD than to put confidence in princes.
All nations compassed me about: but in the name of the LORD will I destroy them.
They compassed me about; yea, they compassed me about: but in the name of the LORD I will destroy them.
They compassed me about like bees; they are quenched as the fire of thorns: for in the name of the LORD I will destroy them.
Thou hast thrust sore at me that I might fall: but the LORD helped me.
The LORD is my strength and song, and is become my salvation.
The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tabernacles of the righteous: the right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly.
The right hand of the LORD is exalted: the right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly.
I shall not die, but live, and declare the works of the LORD .
The LORD hath chastened me sore: but he hath not given me over unto death.
Open to me the gates of righteousness: I will go into them, and I will praise the LORD :
This gate of the LORD , into which the righteous shall enter.
I will praise thee: for thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation.
The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.
This is the LORD’s doing; it is marvellous in our eyes. …: Heb. from the LORD
This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
Save now, I beseech thee, O LORD : O LORD , I beseech thee, send now prosperity.
Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD : we have blessed you out of the house of the LORD .
God is the LORD , which hath shewed us light: bind the sacrifice with cords, even unto the horns of the altar.
Thou art my God, and I will praise thee: thou art my God, I will exalt thee.
O give thanks unto the LORD ; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

ai_explanation_en: The people are called to thank God for His goodness and His enduring kindness, especially for the good He has done for them.
Israel is called to say that God's kindness endures forever.
The house of Aaron, meaning the priests who serve in God's Temple, is called to acknowledge that God's kindness endures forever.
Those who fear God are also called to join in thanking Him for His enduring kindness.
The psalmist describes distress and pressure in which the boundaries of his life were closing in. He called to God, and God answered by giving his life room to expand.
When God is with a person, there is no reason to fear, because no human being can ultimately prevail against him.
God is beside the psalmist together with his helpers and warriors, and he will see the downfall of his enemies.
It is better to take refuge in God than to trust in a human being, because God is stronger and more faithful.
It is better to take refuge in God than to trust in nobles, meaning wealthy people of high status.
The psalmist describes being besieged or attacked by armies from every side, but he trusts in God's name and believes he will crush and destroy his enemies.
The enemies surrounded him on every side, but trust in God's name gives him confidence that he will crush them.
The enemies surrounded him like bees attacking someone who approaches their hive. They were subdued and faded quickly like a fire of thorns, through trust in God's name.
The enemy pushed the psalmist and tried to make him fall, but God helped him, and therefore he did not fall.
God is the psalmist's strength and song; his power comes from Him and his praise is directed toward Him, and God became his salvation.
In the tents of the righteous, sounds of joy and salvation are heard because of God's deliverance. God's strong hand succeeds and prevails.
God's right hand is exalted and lifted high, and it acts with strength and success.
The psalmist asks not to die but to live, so that he can tell and publicize God's deeds.
God disciplined the psalmist, but did not hand him over to death.
The psalmist asks that the gates of righteousness be opened to him, so that he may enter the Temple and thank God publicly, increasing recognition of His name.
He is answered that this is the gate of God, and that the righteous, who have emerged vindicated and victorious, will enter it to give thanks to God.
The entering righteous person thanks God for answering his prayer and becoming his salvation.

The stone rejected by the builders because it did not seem suitable eventually became the chief corner stone, in a central and prominent place. Thus it became clear that what had seemed unimportant was a major factor in the salvation.
This reversal came from God, and it is wondrous and beyond their understanding.
The day of salvation is a day that God made, and therefore the people are called to rejoice and be glad in it, or in God.
After thanks for the salvation that has already occurred comes a request for the future: that God save the people, grant success, and bless their path.
The person entering the Temple gate is welcomed in God's name, and the priests or others bless those who come from the Temple.
All proclaim that God has given them light and brought them from darkness and distress into light. They are instructed to bind the festival offering and bring it to the horns of the altar.
The psalmist again thanks God: God is his deity, and he will exalt His name.
The psalm ends with a call to thank God for His goodness and His enduring kindness, just as it began.

ideas.summary_en: The psalm opens with a general call to thank God for His goodness and kindness, then addresses Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear God.
